jobs.title: Academic Tutor at Mateo Tutoring
jobs.description: Employer: Mateo Tutoring Expires: 11/21/2026 About UsMateo Tutoring is a San Francisco-based tutoring and college advising company founded in 2020. We specialize in one-on-one academic support for students across all grade levels, built around each student's goals, learning preferences, and personality.Our approach is what we call the Mateo Method: a three-stage process of Consultation, Pairing, and Scholar Growth. Every student is matched with an educator who fits them. Not just by subject, but by how they think, connect, and teach. We take that match seriously, and we want tutors who do too. The RoleWe are looking for Academic Tutors to join our growing team in the Daly City area. Sessions are one-on-one, conducted weekly in-person, and scheduled around your availability.We cover all grade levels and a wide range of subjects. Common areas include Math, English, Biology, Physics, Chemistry, and Spanish, but we love building a team with range. Whether you specialize in one subject or can confidently teach across several, there is a place for you here.We do not hand tutors a fixed curriculum. Instead, we build personalized learning plans collaboratively. You and founder Lariel work together to design an approach tailored to that specific student. For students focused on keeping up with their coursework, sessions follow the student's existing school material. You will be paired with students whose needs, schedule, and personality align with yours. What We Are Looking For: Strong subject knowledge in at least one academic areaGenuine curiosity and the ability to connect with studentsPatience, warmth, and a non-judgmental approachReliability and clear communicationCurrently enrolled in or a graduate of a four-year universityCompensation:Starting at $25/hour. Sessions are conducted weekly on an hourly basis. How to Apply: Apply directly through Handshake. We will reach out to schedule a brief 15-minute Zoom call to get to know you and discuss the role further.We look forward to meeting you! Get in Touch: email: mateotutoringllc@gmail.comwebsite: mateotutoring.comIG: @mateotutoringllc

jobs.description: Employer: The SEED Schools Expires: 11/22/2026 About The SEED School of Washington, D.C.The SEED Foundation (www.seedfoundation.com) was created in 1997 to establish college-preparatory urban boarding schools that prepare secondary students, both academically and socially, for success in college and beyond. In 1998, the Foundation opened The SEED Public Charter School of Washington, D.C. – the nation’s first public college preparatory boarding school. The school currently serves 250 students in grades 9-12. In 2015, 100% of SEED’s seniors were accepted to a four-year college or university. All SEED students live on campus from Sunday evening through Friday afternoon when they return home for the weekend. The dormitories are organized into small “houses” of an average of 15-18 students per resident advisor for afternoon and evening routines such as academic study hall, house meetings, SPARKS, and other structured activities. We provide a safe and caring 24-hour boarding experience. Our relationship with parents/guardians is essential to the success of their scholar while at SEED. About The SEED Network: SEED is the pioneering national network of public, college-preparatory boarding schools, offering a unique 24-hour, 5-day per week learning environment. Our tuition-free schools, the first of their kind in the U.S., are intentionally designed to serve traditionally underserved students. Supported by The SEED Foundation, we operate in Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Miami, and Los Angeles. The Foundation's College Transition & Success (CTS) team provides comprehensive support to SEED graduates from junior year through college graduation. SEED's success has gained recognition from media outlets like 60 Minutes and The New York Times, and former President Obama has lauded it as "a true success story." Learn more at www.seedfoundation.com. Position Overview: The SEED School of Washington D.C. (SEED DC) is looking for a Math teacher to provide specific instruction in Algebra I through Pre-calculus to provide instruction that promotes and progresses students through High School Math standards to prepare them for the next level and college level coursework. The Math teacher will create an atmosphere that fosters active student participation in the learning process. Instruction should be balanced, giving students an equal opportunity to learn the conceptual understanding as well as the procedural understandings of the math content. methodologies, curriculum resources and materials.Examine student assessment data to inform decision making and to guide and improve instruction.Promote high levels of learning in an engaging and all learners.Plan, organize and deliver appropriate lessons for assigned area(s) of responsibility, and submit lesson plans to the principal on an as requested basis.Establish and maintain a classroom atmosphere conducive to learning.Collaborate with fellow teachers on planning, professional development, and standards-based curriculum and common assessment design to contribute to the continuous improvement of instruction at the school.Assess students’ learning in a professional manner and communicate students’ progress to parents and fellow teachers to facilitate future instruction.Identify jobs.title: Clinical Therapist (Part-Time, with Full-Time Potential) at Project inMOTION
jobs.description: Employer: Project inMOTION Expires: 11/22/2026 Job Title: Clinical Therapist (Part-Time, with Full-Time Potential) Focus: Creative Arts & Movement-Based Therapy Credentials Required: LMSW, LMHC, LCAT, LCSW, LMFT, or comparable New York State credential; limited permit candidates accepted where applicable. Location: 563 West 170th Street, New York, NY 10032 Employment Type: Part-Time, Hourly, with Potential for Full-Time Employment and Benefits Compensation: $30-45 per hour, based on experience, licensure/certification, and qualifications. About Project inMOTION Project inMOTION is dedicated to providing compassionate, inclusive, and culturally responsive mental health and wellness services. Our approach integrates relationship-based, movement-informed care with traditional therapeutic practices to support emotional and social well-being. We primarily serve young people ages 2–30, including neurodivergent individuals and individuals with disabilities, creating a safe and supportive environment for growth and development. Position Summary We are seeking a part-time, hourly Clinical Therapist who is passionate about thinking outside the box when it comes to healing and values movement, creativity, and relational work as essential clinical tools. This role is ideal for clinicians with backgrounds or strong interests in dance/movement therapy, art therapy, music therapy, play therapy, somatic work, and other creative and embodied approaches. The therapist will develop and maintain a clinical caseload, providing individual and group therapy while integrating creative, movement-based, and relationship-centered interventions. This position begins as part-time, hourly employment. Once the clinician establishes a full clinical caseload, the position will transition to full-time employment with benefits. During the part-time period, compensation will be based on the established hourly rate, and scheduled hours will reflect assigned clinical services and other job responsibilities. Upon reaching a full caseload, the clinician will transition to a full-time role with access to applicable employee benefits in accordance with organizational policies and eligibility requirements. We are looking for a clinician who is excited to grow with Project inMOTION, contribute to our collaborative team, and help expand access to innovative, inclusive mental health services. Key Responsibilities: 1. Clinical Services (Core Focus) ● Provide individual and group therapy using creative, movement-based, and experiential approaches. ● Maintain a caseload (individual and/or group), based on program needs. ● Conduct intake assessments and develop individualized, strengths-based treatment plans. ● Integrate modalities such as movement, play, expressive arts, and somatic practices into clinical work. ● Support clients in building emotional awareness, regulation, and social connection through engagement-based interventions. ● Monitor progress and adapt treatment plans to meet evolving client needs. ● Maintain timely, high-quality clinical documentation. ● Participate in supervision to deepen clinical insight and creative practice. 2. Family Support & Psychoeducation ● Conduct family sessions as needed to provide psychoeducation and guidance. ● Support caregivers in understanding client needs and implementing strategies at home. ● Collaborate with families to reinforce treatment goals and promote consistency across environments. 3. Group & Experiential Programming ● Facilitate or co-facilitate movement-based, play-based, or expressive/creative arts group sessions. ● Collaborate with play support staff and other facilitators to bring sessions to life. ● Help design and implement engaging, developmentally appropriate group experiences. 4. Care Coordination ● Collaborate with families, schools, and external providers as clinically indicated. ● Support clients and caregivers with resources, psychoeducation, and skill-building strategies. ● Work closely with PIM’s interdisciplinary team to provide holistic care. 5. Documentation & Compliance ● Maintain accurate and compliant documentation aligned with NYS regulations, PIM guidelines and ethical standards. ● Support billing and insurance processes as needed. 6. Crisis Intervention ● Respond to client crises with appropriate clinical care and professionalism. ● Develop and implement safety and crisis management plans when needed. ● Follow all PIM protocols and communicate with supervisors appropriately. 7. Professional Development & Culture ● Engage in ongoing learning around creative arts therapies, neurodiversity-affirming care, and embodied practices. ● Participate in supervision, team meetings, and case consultations. ● Contribute to a playful, inclusive, and growth-oriented team culture. Who You Are: ● A clinician who believes therapy can happen through movement, play, and creativity not just conversation. ● Comfortable being active, expressive, and flexible in your clinical style. ● Interested in working with neurodivergent individuals and those with developmental differences. ● Collaborative, curious, and open to innovative approaches to care. Qualifications: ● Master’s degree in social work, counseling, or related field. ● Valid NYS licensure or limited permit (LMSW,LCSW, LMHC, LCAT, LMFT, or equivalent). ● Experience providing individual and/or group therapy. ● Background or strong interest in creative arts or movement-based modalities preferred (e.g., dance/movement therapy, art therapy, music therapy, play therapy, somatic practices). ● Experience working with neurodivergent populations is strongly preferred. ● Strong interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills. ● Experience with crisis intervention and care coordination. ● English required; Spanish fluency strongly preferred (other languages include American Sign Language) ● Commitment to ethical, culturally responsive,

jobs.title: First-Year Admissions Counselor at Shenandoah University
jobs.description: Employer: Shenandoah University Expires: 11/22/2026 Shenandoah University’s Office of Admissions is accepting applications for a First-Year Admissions Counselor. This is a full-time benefited position located on our main campus in Winchester, Virginia.The First-Year Admissions Counselor manages all activities necessary to recruit students, within a designated territory, to Shenandoah University in order to meet individual and team enrollment goals. Counselors must have or acquire substantial knowledge about their territory, exercise discretion and independent judgment in developing recruitment strategies for their designated territories and provide a high quality of service to prospective students and families throughout the recruitment, application and acceptance/enrollment processes.The admissions counselor will often be the prospective student’s first contact with the university and must recognize the importance of building a relationship based on the professional, correct, and timely exchange of information. The admissions counselor is also a liaison between prospective families and the faculty and staff of other university departments. In this role, the admissions counselor will be responsible for general recruitment of all academic programs. The ability and willingness to work among a team, independently, and until the task is completed successfully, is essential.Primary responsibilities:Working collaboratively as a member of the First-Year Recruitment team, admissions counselors will be expected to utilize past and current data to analyze the impact, progress, and effectiveness of prior recruitment strategies and events within their designated territories, and then exercise their discretion and independent judgment to create, implement and execute individual recruitment strategies for the upcoming season within their designated territories.Counselors will propose and make adjustments to prior years’ recruitment strategies and events schedules, including discontinuing, modifying or relocating previously held events. jobs.title: Child Care Coalition Facilitator - CED Corps Member at Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
jobs.description: Employer: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan Expires: 11/22/2026 CEDAM is seeking ten CED Corps members for the 2026-27 program year to be placed within host organizations in Michigan to effect positive change for residents, gain community development and economic development experience, and lead impactful local projects. CED Corps members will serve full time in their host organizations during their 11 month term starting October 2026. This position description is for a CED Corps position with Develop Iosco, Inc. as a Child Care Coalition Facilitator.About the Host Organization: Join Develop Iosco and help shape the future of child care across rural Northeast Michigan. The CED Corps will support and facilitate the 11-county Sunrise Side Regional Child Care Coalition, bringing together child care business owners, families, employers, and community partners to turn local needs into regional solutions. This is an opportunity to gain hands-on community economic development experience while helping build a sustainable, community-anchored early childhood system that strengthens families, businesses, and rural communities.CED Corps Member Role and Responsibilities: ● Facilitate and coordinate the 11-county Sunrise Side Regional Child Care Coalition, including Coalition meetings, workgroups, partner communication, follow-up, and implementation of identified priorities. ● Engage child care business owners, parents and families, employers, and community partners through direct outreach, meetings, surveys, and community conversations to ensure regional strategies reflect local needs and experiences. ● Support the transition from short-term child care pilot projects to sustainable regional strategies by helping develop partnerships, identify resources, coordinate projects, and advance long-term sustainability efforts. ● Strengthen communication and collaboration across the 11-county region by connecting partners with resources, sharing information and opportunities, documenting progress, and helping communities learn from one another. ● Support implementation and evaluation of Coalition initiatives by tracking activities and outcomes, assisting with grant-funded projects and reporting, and helping translate Coalition priorities into actionable projects that strengthen child care businesses and improve access to affordable, high-quality care. ● Participate in CED Corps member development through shared learning and collaboration activities, including an in-person orientation and final gathering. The CED Corps will also meet for monthly virtual trainings, and are expected to participate in one National Day of Service during their term.Evaluation and and Reporting: ● Members will complete midpoint and final evaluations over the course of their service term. ● Members will also submit bi-weekly timesheets, monthly reports, and quarterly narrative reports.Preferred Qualifications: The appropriate candidate will have a desire for service, strong interest and/or background in community economic development, planning, coalition building and/or community organizing, and communications or a combination of such interests. The appropriate candidate must possess strong verbal and written communication skills, excellent attention to detail, the ability to work within a team or as an individual and be familiar with the Microsoft Office suite and Google Applications. CED Corps members are required to work the standard office hours of their host organizations.The following skills are required of all members: No specific background or degree is required of CED Corps members! But a minimum of 2 years of experience in these types of situations in conjunction with some post secondary education is essential for success: ● Experience facilitating a meeting with people who have more experience than them ● Complete their work without someone reminding them to do it ● Experience overcoming obstacles in work situations in the past ● Experience managing multiple professional relationships ● Comfortable working outside of the typical 9 am - 5 pm to attend community events ● Ability to use or teach oneself new software in a fast-paced role with little oversightMinimum Qualifications: ● Be 17 years or older at the start of service (no upper age limit) ● Pass a national service criminal history check ● Hold one of the following citizenship statuses: US citizen, US national, or Lawful Permanent Resident ● CED Corps members must have their own means of travel within their community.Compensation: Members will receive a living allowance of $40,000 distributed in even increments, bi-weekly. Members will receive student loan forbearance for qualified loans, health care benefits, child care assistance upon eligibility, and continual professional development. Upon successful completion of service, an education award in the amount of $7,395 will be issued. Members will serve approximately 40 hours per week (a total of 1,700 hours during the service term). This position requires some statewide travel for CEDAM-required events & training; mileage to and from CEDAM required events will be reimbursed by CEDAM.

jobs.description: Employer: The SEED Schools Expires: 11/22/2026 Applicants should apply if interested in teaching any of the following: Biology, Anatomy and Physiology, Chemistry, and Physics About The SEED School of Washington, D.C. The SEED Foundation (www.seedfoundation.com) was created in 1997 to establish college-preparatory urban boarding schools that prepare secondary students, both academically and socially, for success in college and beyond. In 1998, the Foundation opened The SEED Public Charter School of Washington, D.C. – the nation’s first public college preparatory boarding school. The school currently serves 250 students in grades 9-12. In 2015, 100% of SEED’s seniors were accepted to a four-year college or university. All SEED students live on campus from Sunday evening through Friday afternoon when they return home for the weekend. The dormitories are organized into small “houses” of an average of 15-18 students per resident advisor for afternoon and evening routines such as academic study hall, house meetings, SPARKS, and other structured activities. We provide a safe and caring 24-hour boarding experience. Our relationship with parents/guardians is essential to the success of their scholar while at SEED. About The SEED Network: SEED is the pioneering national network of public, college-preparatory boarding schools, offering a unique 24-hour, 5-day per week learning environment. Our tuition-free schools, the first of their kind in the U.S., are intentionally designed to serve traditionally underserved students. Supported by The SEED Foundation, we operate in Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Miami, and Los Angeles. The Foundation's College Transition & Success (CTS) team provides comprehensive support to SEED graduates from junior year through college graduation. SEED's success has gained recognition from media outlets like 60 Minutes and The New York Times, and former President Obama has lauded it as "a true success story." Learn more at www.seedfoundation.com. Position Overview: The SEED School of Washington, D.C. (SEED DC) is looking for a Secondary Science teacher to provide specific instruction in Physics, Biology, and/or Chemistry to provide instruction that promotes and progresses students through High School Science content standards to prepare them for the next level and college level coursework. The Science teacher will create an atmosphere that fosters active student participation in the learning process. Instruction should be balanced, giving students an equal opportunity to learn the conceptual understanding as well as the procedural understandings of the math content. improvement of instruction at the school.Assess students’ learning in a professional manner and communicate students’ progress to parents and fellow teachers to facilitate future instruction.Identify as necessary.Participate in faculty meetings, workshops, staff development programs, and other school sponsored activities.Communicate with administration and parents, as necessary.Assist in data jobs.title: Associate Director of College Counseling (part-time) at Georgetown Day School
jobs.description: Employer: Georgetown Day School Expires: 11/22/2026 About the SchoolGeorgetown Day School opened its doors in 1945 as the first integrated school in a segregated city. GDS was founded by seven changemaker families who envisioned a school committed not only to academic excellence and educational innovation but also to respect and care for others. Believing that diversity is a critical foundation for the most transformational learning, they established a school where all children would be welcomed, celebrated, and challenged to be their best selves.Today, the School’s philosophy and programs strongly reflect its roots. GDS fosters a community of belonging while lifting up every student’s unique gifts, building in each the capacity for compassion, leadership, and creating positive change. 1125 engaged and talented PK-12 students across three divisions love to learn and learn to change the world in GDS’s exciting urban campus with its outstanding facilities. Recognized as one the most dynamic educational institutions in our capital city and nation, GDS today is in a uniquely attractive position, with a deeply-felt and lived history, clear mission, and genuine openness to the possibilities that lie ahead. About the Position DEPARTMENT: High School College Counseling REPORTS TO: Director of College CounselingSUPERVISES: N/AFLSA: ExemptTYPE OF ROLE: Part-time START DATE: January 2027 (or sooner)COMPENSATION: $ 45,000 - $58,000 annually (based on experience)BENEFITS: EligibleApplications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and preference will be given to early applications. Georgetown Day School, an independent day school in Washington, D.C., invites applications for an Associate Director of College Counseling. The College Counseling team at GDS is a mission-driven, collaborative group that guides students and families through the college process with a focus on equity, wellness and balance. Our philosophy of equitable and accessible college counseling centers on student empowerment, self-advocacy and authentic self-reflection. The Associate Director will work as part of a team, expertly guiding students to identify colleges and universities that match their goals and values, developing strong relationships with students and families, and providing sound advice at every step of the college process. As a diverse, inclusive school devoted to preparing our students to live and work in an increasingly globalized and multicultural society, GDS is particularly interested in professionals with demonstrated interest and experience in working in such a school setting. Primary Duties and Responsibilities Advise and support approximately 18 students through all phases of the college process. Counseling students and families with empathy and compassion through the stresses and challenges of the college search, application and enrollment process.Play a key role in the development of an inclusive and forward-thinking college counseling program in collaboration with school leadership.Write detailed, personal and incisive letters of recommendation in support of counselees.Communicate clearly and effectively with students and parents on all issues and trends related to college admissions, standardized testing and financial aid.Work closely with the College Counseling team to organize and run college counseling events and to develop new programming.Stay abreast of new programs and policies at colleges and universities through professional conferences, college tours, networking and reading of relevant publications.Develop and maintain strong relationships with admissions officers at a wide array of colleges and universities.Represent GDS (its curriculum, mission and students) to colleges and universities in a manner that highlights the unique attributes of a GDS education. Participate fully in the life of the school through faculty meetings, in-service learning opportunities, and academic advising. Secondary Duties and Responsibilities Additional duties outside this description may be assigned as necessary. Qualifications Education and ExperienceB.A. or B.S. degree is required.A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in selective college admissions or college counseling is required. Required SkillsExcellent communication skills - be a strong writer, a compelling speaker, a thoughtful listener, and have strong time-management skills. Displays empathy, flexibility, maturity, optimism, and a strong work ethic will be highly valued in this position. Energy to thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced office environment that encourages collaboration, mutual respect, compassion, and care. As an inclusive school devoted to preparing our students to live, work, and lead in an increasingly globalized and multicultural society, GDS is particularly interested in professionals with demonstrated interest and experience in working in such a school setting and is driven by the core charge of working to enhance and bring joy to every student’s individual learning experience in equitable and meaningful ways.

jobs.description: Employer: Hope for Youth and Families Expires: 11/22/2026 Reading Intervention TeacherOrganization: Hope for Youth and Families Location: Partner School — Springfield, Massachusetts Position Type: Part-Time, 20-25 hours per week Anticipated Start Date: November/December 2026 Anticipated End Date: June 30, 2027 Compensation:$25 - $30/hour, commensurate with experience and qualifications Reports To: Director of LiteracyAbout Hope for Youth and FamiliesHope for Youth and Families is a nonprofit organization committed to supporting young people and families through educational, enrichment, and community-based programming. We partner with schools and other community organizations to provide students with the support, skills, and opportunities they need to succeed.Hope for Youth and Families seeks a dedicated, experienced educator with an MA Teaching License, or who is working toward one, to serve as a Reading Support Interventionist at a partner school in Springfield, Massachusetts.Position OverviewThe Reading Support Interventionist will provide targeted reading instruction and support to students while working collaboratively with English and Humanities teachers, school staff, and a college intern. The ideal candidate will have classroom teaching experience, a strong background in reading instruction, and knowledge of the Science of Reading and evidence-based literacy practices.This position is ideal for an educator who is passionate about helping students develop foundational and advanced reading skills, improve literacy outcomes, and build confidence as readers and learners.The Reading Intervention Teacher will work approximately 20-25 hours per week during the 2026–2027 school year.Key ResponsibilitiesProvide targeted, small-group and/or individualized reading instruction based on student needs. Assess student reading skills and use assessment data to inform instruction and intervention. Implement evidence-based literacy instruction aligned with the Science of Reading. Support students in developing skills in areas such as Phonological and phonemic awareness, phonics and word recognition, fluency, vocabulary, reading comprehension, background knowledge, and language development, as appropriate. Collaborate regularly with English and Humanities teachers to align reading intervention with classroom instruction and student needs. Support the development and implementation of individualized instructional goals for students. Monitor student progress and maintain accurate records of student participation, instructional goals, and growth. Communicate regularly with school and program staff regarding student progress and instructional needs. Collaborate with and guide a college intern supporting literacy instruction and student learning. Create a positive, supportive, and inclusive learning environment that encourages students to take academic risks and build confidence. Participate in relevant staff meetings, professional development, and program planning. Maintain professional relationships with students, families, school personnel, nonprofit staff, and community partners. Perform other related responsibilities as assigned.Required QualificationsIn progress toward obtaining a Massachusetts teaching license in an appropriate area, such as English Language Arts, Reading, Moderate Disabilities, or another relevant licensure area. Experience supporting reading, literacy, English Language Arts, or providing reading intervention. Demonstrated knowledge of the Science of Reading and evidence-based reading instruction, or willingness to learn. Experience working with middle school and/or high school students. Strong communication, collaboration, and organizational skills. Ability to work effectively as part of a collaborative team. Commitment to supporting students with diverse learning needs, backgrounds, and experiences. Ability to work approximately 20-25 hours per week for the program period.Preferred QualificationsMassachusetts teaching license in an appropriate area, such as English Language Arts, Reading, Moderate Disabilities, or another relevant licensure area. Experience providing structured literacy or reading intervention. Experience using student data and assessment information to inform instruction. Training or experience in evidence-based literacy programs and instructional approaches. Experience working with students who have reading difficulties or significant gaps in literacy skills. Experience collaborating with English, Humanities, special education, or intervention teachers. Experience mentoring or supervising college students, interns, tutors, or paraprofessionals. Knowledge of adolescent literacy development. Experience working in an urban school or community-based educational setting. Familiarity with progress monitoring and literacy assessment tools.Ideal CandidateThe ideal candidate is an experienced and reflective educator who:Believes all students can become stronger readers with effective, explicit, and appropriately targeted instruction. Understands the importance of evidence-based literacy practices. Can build strong relationships with students while maintaining high expectations. Is collaborative, flexible, and comfortable working across nonprofit and school-based settings. Can translate reading data into meaningful instructional decisions. Enjoys working with adolescents and supporting students who may have experienced frustration or difficulty with reading. Is committed to equity and ensuring students have access to the literacy skills needed for success in school, college, careers, and life.Compensation and ScheduleCompensation: $25-30/hour, commensurate with experience and qualifications.Schedule: Approximately 20-25 hours per week, 7:30AM - 12:30PM (minimally flexible)Anticipated Employment Period: November/December 2026 – June 30, 2027.The position's 20-25 hour workweek is expected to include direct student instruction, instructional planning and preparation, collaboration with English and Humanities teachers, student assessment and progress monitoring, meetings, and collaboration with the college intern.To ApplyPlease submit the following:Resume Cover letter describing your experience with reading instruction and the Science of Reading; copy or documentation of current Massachusetts teaching licensure; three professional references, including email & phone numberApplications may be submitted to Sami@hyff.org.Hope for Youth and Families is committed to creating an inclusive and supportive environment for students, staff, and community members. We encourage qualified candidates with diverse experiences and backgrounds to apply.

The VHCB AmeriCorps program supports the innovative dual-goal approach of creating stable affordable housing opportunities for Vermont residents while preserving the natural and working landscape. jobs.description: Employer: Neuhaus Education Center Expires: 11/22/2026 Dyslexia Intervention Fellow (Part-Time)Do you love teaching kids to read? Have you dreamed of building a career as a certified dyslexia therapist — without taking on the cost of getting there? If you get a thrill out of watching a struggling reader finally crack the code, keep reading — this could be exactly the opportunity you’ve been looking for. For over 40 years, Neuhaus has been a leader in structured literacy education, teacher training, and dyslexia intervention. Through its programs, Neuhaus empowers educators, supports families, and transforms outcomes for students with reading difficulties and dyslexia. To learn more about us, check out our website neuhaus.org! Location of Position: Bellaire, TX – In-Office RoleSchedule: Monday–Thursday, 3:00–6:00 PM The Position: The Dyslexia Reading Tutor/Intern is a paid, hands-on pathway into a career as a certified dyslexia therapist. You’ll deliver direct reading intervention and literacy enrichment to students with dyslexia while receiving fully funded training, mentorship, and practicum hours toward your CALP or C-SLDI certification. It’s the ideal next step for anyone ready to turn a love of teaching reading into a lasting career in literacy and dyslexia intervention.Position Responsibilities: Deliver structured literacy tutoring and reading intervention to K–12 students in small groups and one-on-one settings.Lead engaging reading and writing enrichment activities that build on daily dyslexia therapy sessions.Complete paid coursework, practicum hours, and supervised training toward CALP or C-SLDI certification.Track and celebrate student progress, using data to inform instruction and demonstrate measurable reading gains.Collaborate with certified dyslexia therapists, specialists, and Neuhaus staff to strengthen your own instructional skills.Contribute to community outreach, professional workshops, and dyslexia-awareness events.Represent Neuhaus Education Center professionally with students, families, and colleagues.Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications: Actively pursuing or holding a bachelor’s degree in liberal arts, communication, education, or a related field required.Strong personal reading, spelling, and writing skills, without the use of AI.Evidence of student-facing experience (e.g., tutoring, mentoring, youth programs, etc.) preferred.Desired Skills and Competencies: Passionate about literacy instruction and supporting students with dyslexia.Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.Technologically proficient and able to work effectively in remote and hybrid environments with internal and external teams. Why You Should Apply: Fully funded training, mentorship, and practicum hours toward CALP or C-SLDI dyslexia therapist certification — at no cost to you.A meaningful first step if you’re not sure what’s next — no education background required, just a love of working with kids and a willingness to learn.A clear, structured path from Dyslexia Intervention Fellow into a licensed, in-demand career as a certified dyslexia therapist.Direct mentorship from experienced, certified dyslexia therapists and CALT-QI instructors invested in your growth.The chance to watch a struggling reader build real confidence and make measurable progress — the kind of impact that lasts.Be part of a nationally recognized nonprofit that has led the field in structured literacy and dyslexia intervention for over 40 years.A part-time schedule that can work around school or other commitments. jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow at Hennepin Healthcare Research Institute
jobs.description: Employer: Hennepin Healthcare Research Institute Expires: 11/22/2026 Post-Doctoral Research Fellowship at the Hennepin Healthcare Research Institute (HHRI) andthe Department of Surgery at Hennepin HealthcareThe Hennepin Healthcare Research Institute (HHRI) is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the spinal cord injury (SCI) neuromodulation program of the Neurosurgery Restorative Neurotrauma Lab, with joint appointments at the University of Minnesota. The lab runs one of the largest active portfolios of epidural and transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation studies in the country, including the E-STAND trial, long-term outcomes follow-up of implanted participants, home-based and rhythm-based stimulation protocols, and a new noninvasive transcutaneous stimulation line. Our work spans restoration of volitional movement, autonomic function (cardiovascular, bladder, bowel, and sexual function), and data-driven optimization of stimulation parameters.The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will work directly with the Principal Investigators as a scientific writing and analysis partner: leading manuscripts from existing datasets, drafting and assembling grant applications, and analyzing electrophysiological, kinematic, and autonomic data. The Fellow will also support the day-to-day science of the lab by participating in stimulation sessions, helping refine protocols, and mentoring graduate students and trainees. This position is well suited to a candidate who intends to build an independent research program in neuromodulation and wants a productive, data-rich environment in which to publish and write.This is a 50/50 hybrid role requiring a minimum of 50% onsite presence in downtown Minneapolis, MN.ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:Under the direction of the Principal Investigators, work closely with HCMC/HHRI investigators to define research questions, analyses, and data elements for spinal cord injury neuromodulation projects.Scientific writing: lead and co-author manuscripts from ongoing SCI studies; draft specific aims, significance, approach, and preliminary data sections for federal (NIH, DoD) and foundation grant applications; prepare progress reports, abstracts, and conference presentations. (35%)Data analysis: analyze surface EMG, kinematic/accelerometer, cardiovascular, and autonomic time-series data; build and maintain reproducible analysis pipelines in Python and/or MATLAB; produce publication-quality figures and statistical analyses. (30%)Study and lab support: participate in stimulation and assessment sessions; contribute to protocol design, amendments, and IRB submissions; support REDCap database structure and data quality; help coordinate device programming and stimulation parameter optimization workflows. (25%)Mentorship and collaboration: mentor graduate students and trainees on analysis and writing; work within a multidisciplinary team; contribute to collaborations with the University of Minnesota and external partners. (10%)NON-ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:Collaborate with researchers on projects related to Spinal Cord Injury and Traumatic Brain InjuryEMPLOYMENT STANDARDS:Education/Experience:Doctoral degree (PhD, MD, or equivalent) in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, physiology, rehabilitation science, kinesiology, biostatistics, or a related field.The ideal candidate will have a strong record of scientific writing and previous experience in one or more of the following areas: spinal cord injury, neuromodulation, human electrophysiology, clinical research, or quantitative analysis of physiological time-series data.Skill, Knowledge & Ability (SKA):Requires interaction with a diverse population, including direct contact with research participants with spinal cord injury. Works effectively within a multidisciplinary team of neurosurgeons, engineers, physiologists, coordinators, and rehabilitation clinicians, and collaborates with researchers across the lab's spinal cord injury and traumatic brain injury programs.Minimum qualifications:Doctoral degree (PhD, MD, or equivalent) in a relevant field.Demonstrated writing productivity: first-author peer-reviewed publications and experience contributing to grant applications or fellowship proposals.Strong quantitative skills, including programming in Python and/or MATLAB and experience analyzing time-series physiological data (e.g., EMG, EEG, kinematics, cardiovascular signals).Experience designing, conducting, and interpreting human-subjects research.Clear, efficient written and verbal communication; ability to work independently and manage multiple projects.Display high standards of attendance, punctuality, maintains confidentiality, and manages time effectively.Preferred qualifications:Prior research in spinal cord injury, neuromodulation (epidural, transcutaneous, or other electrical stimulation), or motor/autonomic neurophysiology.Experience with human electrophysiology data acquisition (EMG, EEG, accelerometry) and stimulation hardware.Familiarity with clinical trial conduct, IRB/regulatory processes, and REDCap database building and reporting.Experience with statistical modeling of longitudinal or repeated-measures data and with power/sample-size analysis for grant applications.Interest in autonomic outcomes (cardiovascular, bladder, bowel, sexual function) after spinal cord injury.Track record of, or interest in pursuing, fellowship or career-development funding (e.g., F32, K-series, foundation awards) with PI support.This position will be compensated based on NIH guidelines for post-doctoral roles: $63,480 - $77,076, DOQ.Questions about this position or requests for more detailed information can be directed to Dr. David Darrow at darro015@umn.eduHHRI is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.description: Employer: LearnToBot Expires: 11/22/2026 # Assistant Robotics & Coding Instructor (Part-Time) — West & Southwest HoustonLearnToBot teaches hands-on robotics and coding classes for kids ages 6–15 across the Houston area. Students build with real electronics — sensors, motors, RC cars, robotic arms — write real code, and take everything they build home. We are hiring college-student assistant instructors for our west and southwest Houston classes. This is the entry role: you support the lead instructor, learn our projects, and grow into leading your own classes.## Where you will work — read this firstOur classes run in Katy, Cypress, Sugar Land, Spring/The Woodlands, and Houston. **You must live on the west or southwest side of Houston and be available in those areas.** Our immediate openings include Thursday afternoons at Westbury Christian School in southwest Houston, plus other weekday-afternoon classes nearby.Equipment is stored at Extra Space Storage, 3800 Highway 6 S, Houston. Assistant instructors run equipment pickups and drop-offs too. **A reliable car and a valid driver's license are required for this job.**## The job1. Help the lead instructor run weekly project-based robotics and coding classes for kids ages 6–15 — you work hands-on with students while they build.2. Pick up, transport, and return class equipment between storage and the class location. Driving between storage and class is paid time.3. Set up before class and pack up after; help students who get stuck on a build or a line of code.4. Confirm your shifts in our app, arrive early, and help complete the class report after each class.## Pay and mileage- **$17–$21/hour**, depending on experience, with a clear path to Senior Instructor pay ($18–$25/hour) as you learn to run projects and classes independently.- Mileage: your normal commute is on you. Driving beyond the first 25 miles each way is reimbursed at **$0.76/mile**.- Part-time during the school year; full-time hours available during school holidays and camps.## Who this fits- Current college student (University of Houston students encouraged) in Computer Science, Computer/Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or another STEM field — or a strong tech background without the degree.- Motivated and comfortable with technology. Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, or Python experience is a plus, not a requirement — we train you, and you build every project yourself before helping teach it.- Experience with kids (tutoring, camps, coaching, babysitting) is a plus.- Must pass a background check (required by our school partners).## How to applyIn your application, include:1. The area/neighborhood where you live.2. Whether you have a reliable car.3. Your weekly availability, especially weekday afternoons and Thursdays.Applications without these three answers will not be considered.

jobs.title: Mental Health Case Manager at Denton County MHMR Center
jobs.description: Employer: Denton County MHMR Center Expires: 11/22/2026 Under direction of the Program Manager of Adult Mental Health and within federal, state and local guidelines performs routine case management work. Work involves developing and maintaining long-term contact with clients, client families, and service providers for medical, social, educational, and related service needs.This position is responsible for overseeing the care of individuals served assigned to various Levels of Care (LOC). Works to ensure the continuity of care for individuals served. Works under moderate supervision, with limited latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment.Education, Training, and ExperienceGraduation from an accredited four-year college or university with major course work in a human services field as required to qualify as a Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) and six (6) months prior experience in a mental health field preferred. Master's Degree in a human services field and previous Crisis experience preferred. English/Spanish bilingual preferred.Registration, Certification, Licensure, and Other QualificationsMust have and maintain a background and criminal history free from any disqualifying offenses as outlined by the Texas Administrative Code (TAC) and the Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC).Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license and automobile insurance.o Individuals with an out-of-state driver's license must be able to obtain a driver's license in the state of Texas within thirty (30) days. Successful completion of all position-specific training within thirty (30) days of employment is required.Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Knowledge of community resources, of case management delivery systems, and of program policies and procedures. Ability to assess clients' needs, coordinate individuals' services, communicate effectively, and to train others. Ability to work as a member of an interdisciplinary team to ensure referral to appropriate Center program as needed. Has the ability to work independently and make decisions but seeks guidance when needed. Ability to make decisions based on education and or clinical experience, which reflect consistency with Center's Guiding Principles, Policies and Procedures, and Standards of Care. This position requires an understanding of community resources available for Denton County and the willingness to acquire new resources in the community. Understanding and practice of Trauma Informed Care principles. Ability to work with clients of different cultural backgrounds, sexual orientation, and belief systems. Ability to work with clients who may display symptoms of mental illness including; poor hygiene, difficulty controlling anger and low frustration tolerance, difficulty or inability to display appropriate social behavior, and who are suicidal or homicidal. Ability to display regular and reliable (in-person, if required) attendance.Understanding and practice of Trauma Informed Care principles.Essential DutiesThe following list outlines key responsibilities for the position; however, it is not exhaustive and does not encompass all responsibilities. Additional duties may be assigned as needed.1. Standard and expectation of above function. Attends and participates in all scheduled team meetings. Staff will attend meetings as scheduled and sign in for meetings to acknowledge their presence and understanding of the topics discussed. If a meeting is missed, staff will get with supervisor within one week to review the information.2. Provides courteous, professional services at all times. Maintains professional boundaries. Interacts with Center staff, individuals, and community members in a professional manner.3. Provides Case Management services. . Caseload size will vary. Provide supported employment, supported housing, budgeting, skills training as appropriate, etc., to individuals served as defined in Texas Resilience Recovery (TRR) guidelines. Provides resources/referrals to meet individual needs and helps them navigate different systems. Will assist other teammates in their absence by providing services to individuals on their caseload as needed.4. Completes community base visits per minimum monthly contact. Community based visits to occur 20% of the time for individuals approved for Level of Care (LOC) 1 and LOC 2.5. Provides transportation for individuals as needed.Safely transports individuals using Center vehicles and/or personal vehicle without accident, citation or another incident.Follows all Center guidelines while driving, including restriction of food, drink, smoking, and cell phone use.Completes all required vehicle checklists as scheduled.Maintains fuel and fluid levels of vehicles and reports all maintenance issues immediately to appropriate supervisor.Maintains personal driving record within agency standards and requirements.Provides ongoing evidence of current auto liability insurance.Provides transportation in own vehicle only as approved by supervisory staff.Maintains his or her personal vehicle and company vehicles to ensure the safety of individuals and other staff.Completes vehicle paperwork in a timely manner.Keeps company vehicles clean and disposes of trash and clutter daily.Drives safely and adhere to all Center and state laws.6. Ensures each individual served is provided services as required by the level of care assignment. Engagement measure with consumers is at 65.6% on a monthly basis. Maintains contact standards as defined in TRR guidelines.7. Administers clinical assessments and paperwork to determine appropriateness of level of care assignments and level of rehabilitative services required to meet individual's needs. Required paperwork includes: Adult Needs and Strength Assessment (ANSA), Recovery Plan, Substance Abuse Needs Inventory, Rights Review, TIMA consent forms, Tobacco Cessation Form, and Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (CSSRS) Form completed prior to expiration and as needed based on individual change.8. Is familiar with all applicable Texas Administrative Code (TAC), fidelity tools, and Texas Human Health Services (HHSC) contract information and Center policies and procedures. All documentation is completed within two business days, to meet or exceed 95% monthly. Skills training notes include fidelity words.9. Ensures individuals charts are in compliance with HHSC contract requirements and standards. Responds to all chart audits by assigned deadline. All paperwork will be signed in black ink/or electronically in the EHR with credentials and date. All paperwork is completed within Center policies and procedures.10. Provides emergency/crisis intervention when necessary according to HHSC and Center policies and procedures.11. Completes other duties as assigned.All assignments given are completed in a timely manner.12. Has the ability to work independently and make decisions but seeks guidance when needed13. Participates in the Center's Zero Suicide Initiative.a. Supports individuals experiencing a crisis by promptly connecting them with appropriate Center programs, such as the Mobile Crisis Outreach Team (MCOT), Psychiatric Triage, Crisis Prevention services, and/or other applicable resources. Ensure seamless coordination to facilitate timely intervention.b. Remains with individuals, when deemed safe, to provide support and maintain a calm environment until specialized crisis staff or emergency personnel arrive to take over intervention efforts. Adheres to safety protocols to prevent escalation of the crisis situation.c. Participates in debriefing sessions with the immediate supervisor or designated staff following a crisis event. Collaborate with the team to review the incident, identify lessons learned, and ensure all HHSC guidelines and Center policies are followed.

jobs.description: Employer: Topeka Public Schools USD 501 Expires: 11/22/2026 Position Purpose:The Early Childhood teacher creates and maintains a program that focuses on the physical, social, and emotional development of each child. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Woods & Construction Technology Teacher at Juab School District
jobs.description: Employer: Juab School District Expires: 11/22/2026 Woods & Construction Technology Teacher Juab High School | Juab School District Position Available: January 2027 Juab School District is seeking an enthusiastic and skilled Woods & Construction Technology Teacher to join our team at Juab High School beginning January 2027. We are looking for an individual who is passionate about woodworking, construction, and skilled trades and enjoys sharing their knowledge with the next generation. The ideal candidate will bring practical, real-world experience, strong technical skills, and a commitment to helping students develop valuable career and life skills. We welcome licensed educators as well as experienced industry professionals interested in transitioning into education! Multiple pathways to educator licensure may be available, including options that recognize relevant industry experience, professional certifications, and technical expertise. Teaching Assignments The selected candidate will be responsible for teaching courses that may include: Woodworking / Woods Construction Technology Construction Management Other related Career and Technical Education (CTE) courses as assigned Essential Job Functions Plan, develop, and deliver engaging, hands-on instruction aligned with Utah State Board of Education CTE curriculum standards. Teach students fundamental and advanced woodworking, construction, and building techniques, including the safe operation of hand tools, power tools, and shop equipment. Provide instruction in construction materials, project planning, blueprint reading, measurement, estimating, framing, and building practices. Introduce students to construction management concepts, including project organization, scheduling, budgeting, and quality control. Design and supervise practical projects that allow students to apply classroom knowledge to real-world construction and woodworking experiences. Establish and enforce appropriate safety procedures, including the proper use of personal protective equipment and safe operation of machinery. Maintain a safe, organized, and productive classroom and shop environment. Monitor, maintain, and properly care for tools, machinery, equipment, and instructional materials. Assess student progress through hands-on projects, demonstrations, assignments, and other appropriate evaluation methods. Introduce students to career opportunities in construction, woodworking, carpentry, construction management, and related skilled trades. Collaborate with fellow educators, administrators, and industry professionals to strengthen CTE programs and provide career-connected learning opportunities. Maintain accurate student records, including attendance, grades, and progress. Participate in professional development, faculty meetings, and other school and district activities. Fulfill all professional responsibilities and expectations established by Juab School District. Qualifications Preferred Qualifications: Current Utah Professional Educator License with appropriate CTE endorsements for assigned courses. Professional experience in carpentry, woodworking, residential or commercial construction, construction management, general contracting, or a related skilled trade. Knowledge of construction practices, building materials, tools, machinery, and industry safety standards. Strong communication, organizational, and classroom management skills. Previous teaching or instructional experience is preferred but not required. Alternative Licensure Pathway: Juab School District recognizes the value of real-world industry experience and encourages skilled professionals to explore a career in education. Applicants who do not currently hold a Utah teaching license may qualify through alternative licensing pathways, including: Alternate Pathway to Professional Educator License (APPEL): Individuals with a bachelor's degree in a related field may qualify to pursue educator licensure while teaching and completing an approved preparation program. CTE Occupational Experience Pathway: Individuals with at least 3 years of full-time occupational experience (or the part-time equivalent) in construction, carpentry, woodworking, or related trades may be eligible for CTE licensing and endorsements based on documented industry experience. CTE Competency-Based Endorsements: Individuals with relevant industry certifications, technical training, professional credentials, or demonstrated competencies may qualify for applicable CTE endorsements. Relevant qualifications may include construction or contractor licenses, trade certifications, technical education, documented industry experience, or other credentials recognized by the Utah State Board of Education. Applicants without a bachelor's degree are encouraged to apply if they have substantial industry experience or relevant professional certifications. All candidates must meet applicable Utah State Board of Education licensing and endorsement requirements for their assigned teaching responsibilities. Juab School District will work with qualified candidates to explore applicable licensing pathways. Desired Skills and Attributes Passion for working with high school students and helping them develop practical, career-ready skills. Ability to teach technical concepts through engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Strong commitment to shop safety and responsible equipment operation. Knowledge of current construction practices, industry standards, and emerging technologies. Ability to manage multiple student projects while maintaining a safe and productive learning environment. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build positive relationships with students, colleagues, and families. Willingness to learn, grow professionally, and participate in ongoing educator preparation and training. Juab School District is and equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description: Employer: TRANSITIONS-MENTAL HEALTH ASSOCIATION Expires: 11/22/2026 Employment Opportunity Position Title: Residential Adult Counselor - “Relief” Program/Location: Adult Transitional Program / San Luis Obispo Position Summary:“Recovery can only take place within the context of relationships” –Judith Lewis Herman The Adult Transitional Program (ATP) is a trauma aware transitional housing program that provides 24/7 support to adults with mental illness in a home-like setting. This home is located in downtown San Luis Obispo and houses up to 12 people. Residential Adult Counselors (RAC) provide comprehensive and supportive care to the residents. Interactions are based on trauma informed practices including; safety, power of choice, collaboration, trustworthiness and empowerment. Working in the resident’s home provides an opportunity for staff to build trust based relationships that help each individual to establish a healthy daily routine, effective communication skills, increase independent living skills and to build support based networks in the community that will help them transition to stable independent housing. RAC’s expectations are to: facilitate and model safe and healthy connection, demonstrate integrity and transparency, meet residents where they are at in a nonjudgmental and encouraging way, and promote and teach healthy coping tools to aid in reductions of mental health symptoms. RAC’s help residents increase levels of independent functioning and personal responsibility such as: cooking, cleaning, budgeting, medication management and tracking appointments. RAC’s enjoy opportunities to facilitate recovery-oriented outings and activities such as beach walks, playing games, coffee shop visits, hikes, bowling, and disc golf. We are looking for professionals who have a passion for building healthy, healing community. At ATP our values are: genuine care, supporting resident’s goals, flexible collaboration, and empowering residents to take recovery into their own hands. Learn More About ATPhttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JL2o8edAGVo&t=10s Hours/ Salary Employee Perks:Relief, non-exempt. This position has no guaranteed hours but is coverage for staff vacations and sick time. Shifts can be scheduled ahead of time or be short notice due to staffing needs. Due to the 24/7 nature of the program this position may include some combination of day, weekend, holiday and overnight shifts. Schedules can be flexible and can accommodate a variety of preferences. Day shifts are typically 8-4 or 9-5:30. Overnight shift hours are 4pm-8am with sleeping hours from 12am-6am. Expectation that some holiday shifts will need to be worked. Anticipated hiring is $22.00. We host two employee appreciation events for employees and their families yearly. This position requires in person work for face-to-face contact with residents for every shift. A minimum of 1-year, full-time experience working in a program serving people with co-occurring Mental Health disorders is preferred. Strong interpersonal skills, collaborative work style and strong oral/written and communication skills. Well-defined organizational and time management skills. Ability to work independently and flexibly. Ability to handle intense situations, display good judgment and decision-making skills, and remain calm and clearheaded under pressure. Able to work effectively with a variety of people and personality types regardless of age, ethnicity, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression or socio-economic level. jobs.description: Employer: Goodwill of Southern Nevada Expires: 11/22/2026 ESSENTIAL EXPECTATIONSCustomer Service ExpectationsServing customers at Goodwill has never been more rewarding. Whether serving our guests with their shopping experiences, assisting someone in our community to better their life, or helping your fellow coworker to exceed, Goodwill is about reaching out and making a difference.Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion ExpectationsGoodwill is committed to fostering a culture of dignity and trust where all individuals feel respected and valued. management on service goals being met, grant statistics, etc.Ensures compliance with all applicable policies and procedures.Works on special projects as assigned by the Director of Career Services.Participates in departmental, agency, and community meetings.Ensures best use of technology in support of programmatic objectives and makes recommendations for related improvements.Grant ManagementAssists and leads the team in meeting the required annual enrollment requirements.Collaborates with the grant accountant in meeting spending and invoice monitoring requirements for fund standing, walking, reaching, stooping, lifting, pulling, carrying, sitting at a desk, and working on a computer.

jobs.title: Private Music Teacher at Arabesque Conservatory of Music
jobs.description: Employer: Arabesque Conservatory of Music Expires: 11/22/2026 $32.50 hourly - Part-time.In-person lesson rate increases under the employed structure are scheduled as follows:January 1, 2027 - $35.00 per hourDrive time is paid at $20 per hour + mileage reimbursementAdministrative time is paid at $20 per hour (paid in 15-minute increments)Additional details will be provided during the interviewJoin our vibrant arts/music education team at United Academy of Music & Arts as a Music Coach. We ask that those who apply be able to teach one or more of the following: violin, piano, guitar, drums, and other musical disciplines. *Please note that most learners will be taught at a beginner level. In this role, your passion for the performing arts will inspire and empower students of all ages, including those with special needs, to discover their creative potential. You will lead engaging one-on-one music lessons that may take place in students' homes. While fostering a love for music, you will help nurture confidence and collaboration among learners. Your enthusiasm and expertise will help cultivate a lively, inclusive environment where artistic expression thrives. This paid position offers an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful impact through education and creativity.Duties:Design and deliver engaging performing Music lessons tailored to diverse age groups and skill levelsDevelop innovative curricula that incorporates music using traditional and contemporary instruments such as violin, piano, guitar, drums, and other exciting instruments, along with various artistic disciplines such as signing.Assess student progress regularly and provide constructive feedback to encourage growthMaintain a safe and positive learning environment that promotes artistic exploration and teamworkSupport students in developing technical skills, stage presence, and expressive storytelling techniquesMaintain Professional Standards: Adhere to all organizational guidelines, including safety protocols, company policies, confidentiality requirements, and standards of professional conduct.Travel and Scheduling: Effectively manage a flexible schedule, demonstrating reliability and punctuality when traveling to in-home or community locations and maintaining professionalism in all settings.ExperiencePrevious experience teaching or leading performing arts classes in educational or community settingsProven ability to motivate and engage students of varying ages and backgroundsExperience planning curriculum activities that foster creativity and skill developmentUniversity experience is highly desirable to ensure a well-rounded understanding of arts education principlesExcellent communication skills with the ability to inspire confidence and enthusiasm among studentsA passion for the performing arts coupled with a commitment to fostering inclusive artistic environmentsTimekeeping and Administrative Responsibilities:Attendance Tracking: Take accurate attendance for each online session and document all completed lessons.Time Management: Clock in and out of designated tasks using the company’s scheduling system.Accurate Time Recording: Maintain precise records of teaching and administrative time, ensuring compliance with company policies.Timely Submission: Turn in completed timesheets and any required documentation by established deadlines.Clear Communication: Notify administrative staff promptly of any schedule changes, cancellations, or technical issues affecting lessons.Incident Documentation: Maintain thorough records of any incidents or technical disruptions affecting student engagement or lesson delivery.Additional Duties:Assist with recitals, showcases, and other performance opportunities, providing support and encouragement to students.Collaborate with the administrative team to ensure smooth scheduling and communication with families.Incident Reporting: Promptly report any incidents involving students, including behavioral concerns, safety issues, or emergencies, following company protocols.Mandated Reporting: Recognize and report signs of abuse, neglect, or concerning behaviors in accordance with mandated reporting laws and company policies.Complete other duties as assigned, demonstrating flexibility and a willingness to support the organization's needs.Requirements:Strong musical background, with proficiency in singing, basic piano,drums, or guitar, and knowledge of music theory.Experience teaching or working with young children, including those with special needs.Demonstrated ability to adapt to the unique learning styles and behavioral needs of children with compassion and flexibility.Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to build trust with children and families.Reliable transportation and willingness to travel to students’ homes.Ability to manage a flexible schedule, including occasional evenings or weekends.Must be available and open to working at least 20 hours per week. Actual weekly hours and student assignments may vary based on student demand, location, scheduling compatibility, and successful student/instructor matching.Bi-lingual in Spanish(a plus but not required)Candidates must be willing to undergo a background check as part of the hiring process.Please note that because this position involves driving and working with vulnerable populations, information obtained through the background check process may be considered when evaluating a candidate's suitability. While not all background findings will automatically disqualify a candidate, we maintain strict safety standards and review each case individually based on the nature of the offense, when it occurred, and its relevance to the responsibilities of the position.If you think you meet some of the qualifications, but don't necessarily check every box in the job description, we encourage you to still apply. If you have questions, contact the Recruiting Manager at eparedes@arabesqueconservatory.comWhat We Offer:Competitive hourly pay for teaching time, plus paid driving time and mileage reimbursement.Flexible part-time hours to accommodate your schedule.Opportunities for professional development and growth within the United Academy of Music & Arts.A supportive team environment committed to inclusive and adaptive music education.Job Types: Full-time, Part-timeBenefits:Employee discountReferral programPaid sick timePaid trainingMedical, dental & vision for those that work a min of 30 hours consistentlyMileage reimbursement is paid at 72.5 cents per mile at this time and is per federal guidelinesWe also offer a $150 referral bonus for instructors who refer a new instructor who then teaches at least one lesson.Please note because this position involves driving as an essential function and direct work with vulnerable populations, safety is central to our hiring process. Following a conditional offer of employment, we conduct a background check consistent with California law. If the background check reveals criminal history, we conduct an individualized assessment before making any decision. This includes the nature and gravity of the offense, the time that has passed since the offense or completion of sentence, and its relevance to the duties of this role.Given the driving and direct client-facing responsibilities of this position, the individualized assessment will consider whether any conviction history has a direct and adverse relationship to the specific duties of the position, including responsibilities involving driving, client safety, and work with vulnerable populations.Work Location: In person, On the roadBenefits: Flexible schedulePaid time off Work Location: On the road

Encourage students and colleagues alike to maintain vibrant and continuous artistic exploration, truly embodying CAP’s core value to maintain your creative spark.What You Will BringA Passion for Theatric and Educational Excellence: With a strong background in theatre and experience in theatre education, you are ideally equipped to merge these realms to cultivate high standards of learning and creativity. Creativity and Collaborative Spirit: As a creative problem-solver, you excel in innovating and adapting to foster a supportive community among students, educators and parents. Your strong collaborative spirit enables you to work effectively alongside educational and community members, enhancing the learning environment and maximizing impact through shared efforts and mutual support.Dynamic Educational Approach: Your innovative teaching methods integrate theatre into educational curricula, enhancing student engagement and achievement. Your approach helps students connect with artistic materials in meaningful ways, promoting both artistic skills and broader educational goals. Leadership in Arts Education: You have a proven track record of leading projects that inspire students and educators alike. Your leadership skills are evident in your ability to manage projects, inspire innovation and maintain high educational standards. Resilience and Adaptability: You are adept at navigating the challenges that come with integrating the arts into diverse learning settings. Your resilience helps you adapt lesson plans to meet the needs of various student populations and deliver high-quality educational experiences under varying conditions. Commitment to Students: With a dedication to creating welcoming learning environments, you ensure every child feels valued and empowered to express themselves. Your teaching celebrates a variety of perspectives and encourages students to respect and learn from each other, fostering a rich artistic community.Educational Background: A bachelor’s degree in theatre, arts education or a closely related field is required for this position, with a strong preference for candidates holding an MFA. Ideal candidates will have an educational background that prepares them for profound engagement with theatre and pedagogy and an interest in connecting the arts to history, civics or other core subjects.Professional Experience: You have a demonstrated history of working in theatre, with a specific focus on educating young students. Experience in elementary education is preferred, as this role requires a deep understanding of how to integrate theatre into core curriculum areas, enhancing both artistic development and general educational outcomes. A Day in the LifeMorning Engagement: Start your day energized as you prepare and deliver interactive theatre lessons that seamlessly integrate theatre concepts with other academic subjects, making the content engaging and accessible. Focus on developing lesson plans that blend theatre with academic curriculum goals, ensuring that each session enhances both theatric expression and educational outcomes.Active Collaboration: Spend midday hours engaging with classroom teachers, CAP peers and local arts community members to integrate theatre into the broader curriculum. This collaboration might involve planning upcoming units, discussing student progress and adapting strategies to meet diverse learning needs. Also, focus on strengthening relationships with cultural partners to enhance CAP’s presence and impact within the arts community.Afternoon Creativity: Lead theatre sessions for school lessons, curating enriching opportunities for showcasing student work. Provide students with valuable opportunities to create and present their talents, fostering an environment where they can gain confidence and appreciation for their creative expressions.Community Connection: Occasionally participate in workshops or community arts events, which strengthen the bond between CAP and the wider community. These activities highlight the role the arts play in fostering community engagement and cultural appreciation.Reflection and Planning: Wrap up your day by using data to reflect on the successes and learning opportunities of the day. Plan for future lessons considering how best to address student needs and make the most of the educational experience the next day.Perks & BenefitsCompetitive Compensation: A competitive salary, up to $60,000 based on your experience. This position recognizes the value you bring to CAP and offers the opportunity for annual merit increases of up to 3% and performance bonuses up to 3%.Healthcare Coverage: To ensure you and your health are well taken care of, CAP will cover 75% of the premiums in your selected plan for individual medical, dental and vision insurance options. Retirement Planning: Invest in your future with CAP’s 403(b) retirement savings plan, including a CAP match of up to 3%. It’s never too early or too late to start planning for retirement.Generous Time Off: Recharge and rejuvenate with 21 days of paid time off, plus 24-28 paid holidays throughout the year. CAP’s flexible schedule allows you to balance your professional and personal life effectively.Commuter Benefits: Enjoy paid parking in a central downtown location, making your commute easier. Additionally, receive reimbursement for work-related mileage incurred, supporting your travel needs related to program delivery and community engagement.Professional and Personal Growth: After one year with CAP, you’ll gain access to additional tenured benefits, including opportunities for professional development to further enhance your skills and career. Personal wellness credits are also offered to support your overall well-being.Family First: Following a year of employment, take advantage of CAP’s paid parental/bonding leave, allowing you to focus on your family’s significant life moments. Are You Ready?If you are passionate about making a significant difference through the integration of arts and education and thrive in a role where community and creativity intersect, we invite you to apply. This is more than a job—it’s a chance to be part of something bigger. Join us in shaping the future of arts education! Submit in confidence to Luisa Reis (luisa@capkids.org), VP of Programs, a resume and personal statement of 1,500 words or less explaining a) your personal, artist or educational philosophy statement, b) where you currently are in your career and long-term goals, and c) what unique skills or perspective you will bring to CAP, its students and the Jacksonville community. The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and should not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be performed in the job.
